# ☕ Qahwa — test build

A tiny coffee machine that sits in the corner of your desktop. When an AI gives
you an answer that looks wrong, you drag the coffee cup into the chat box. The AI
receives a file asking it to go back and check its work.

**Windows 10 or 11 only.** There is no Mac version.

## How to install it

1. Download **`Qahwa_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe`** from the Assets list below.
   (Or `Qahwa-portable.exe` if you would rather not install anything — that one
   just runs when you double-click it.)
2. Your browser may say the file "isn't commonly downloaded". Choose **Keep**.
3. Double-click the file. Windows will show a blue box saying
   **"Windows protected your PC"**. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

That blue box is expected. It appears for any program that has not been signed
with a paid certificate, which costs a few hundred dollars a year — it is not a
virus warning. This app was built automatically from public source code, and you
can read every line of it in this repository.

## How to use it

The coffee machine appears in the **bottom-right** of your screen and floats
above your other windows.

1. Open ChatGPT (or Claude) in your browser.
2. Ask it something.
3. If the answer looks off, press and hold on the coffee cup, drag it across into
   the message box, and let go.
4. A file called `☕ Reality Shot.md` appears attached. Send the message.

The AI will re-check its previous answer, separate what it actually knows from
what it assumed, correct anything it got wrong, and say where it is not sure.

- The dotted strip at the top of the window **moves** it.
- The **i** button shows the notice again.
- The **✕** closes it.

## Please tell me

- Did the cup actually drop into the chat box?
- Did the file arrive with the coffee cup emoji in its name?
- Did the little window look right, or was anything cut off or oddly coloured?
- Anything that felt confusing.

## Two things to know

Qahwa asks AI to reconsider and verify its answer. **It can still be wrong.**
Verify important information.

Qahwa does not read or store your conversations. It makes no network calls, keeps
no history, and has no account.
